conventions.convention: Finitary means a supplied small abelian category with finite Hom sets and finite endpoint-fixed Yoneda one-extension sets. Finite-field linearity and finite total subobject sets are not assumed.

[M]*[N] counts subobjects isomorphic to N with quotient isomorphic to M. Coefficients are natural-number counts mapped into the commutative unital coefficient ring, without automorphism denominators or an Euler twist.
The Jordan category uses nilpotent matrices on standard coordinate spaces k^n, including n=0; I_empty is the zero object.
The generic parameter t has degree zero, u_lambda has degree |lambda|, and the generator-normalized isomorphism sends u_(1^r) to t^(-r(r-1)/2)e_r after adjoining t inverse.

Hall–Littlewood functions are monic and downward triangular in dominance, orthogonal for the form with power-sum norm z_lambda times the product of (1-s^lambda_i)^(-1). Empty products and the unit norm are one.
The Jordan Green pairing has diagonal a_lambda(t)^(-1). Its transport in degree d is t^(-d) times the Hall–Littlewood form at s=t^(-1), distinct from the ordinary Hall inner product.

load_bearing.statement: For a finitary abelian category, each untwisted Hall coefficient g^L_(M,N) is finite and depends only on the isomorphism classes of M,N,L. For fixed M,N, only finitely many isomorphism classes [L] have g^L_(M,N) nonzero.

For W ≤ L in an abelian category, inverse image along L → L/W is an order isomorphism from subobjects of L/W to subobjects U ≤ L containing W. The inverse sends U to its image U/W, and (L/W)/(U/W) is canonically isomorphic to L/U.

For every small finitary abelian category A and commutative coefficient ring R, the operation of def-untwisted-hall-algebra is a well-defined associative R-bilinear multiplication on H_(A,R), with unit [0].

Jordan Hall coefficients are universal polynomials in Z[t]. Their generic Hall algebra is a commutative associative unital free polynomial algebra over Z[t] on u_(1^r), r≥1; after adjoining t inverse, u_(1^r) ↦ t^(-r(r-1)/2)e_r gives a graded algebra isomorphism with the correspondingly extended stable symmetric-function ring.
For I_lambda over F_q, |Aut(I_lambda)| = q^(|lambda|+2n(lambda)) times the product over r≥1 and 1≤j≤m_r of (1-q^(-j)); the empty-partition value is one.

For the exact generator-normalized map, Phi_t(u_lambda)=t^(-n(lambda))P_lambda(x;t^(-1)). The transported Green pairing on degree d is t^(-d) times the Hall–Littlewood form at t^(-1), with power-sum norms z_lambda times the product of (t^lambda_i-1)^(-1). The monic orthogonal Hall–Littlewood functions exist uniquely and have norms b_lambda(s)^(-1).

alerts.finding: The final proof step ends with “∎ [step 2.1, step 3.1]”. SCHEMA.md requires the justification tags before the final QED symbol, with only ∎ following the final tag group. This is a proof-formatting defect; the dominance-reversal argument itself supports the cited use.
